items.title: Section: The Five Virtuous-Person Diligences — Never Abandoning, Never Diminishing, Never Faint-Hearted

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士精進？謂此精進略有五種。一、無所棄捨精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，不捨一切欲加行故。二、無退減精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，如先所受若等若增，發勤精進隨長養故。三、無下劣精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，勇猛、熾然、長時、無間精勤策勵，心無怯弱、無退屈故。四、無顛倒精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，能引義利，方便善巧所攝持故。五、勤勇加行精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，能於無上正等菩提達進趣故。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's virtuous-person diligence? This diligence is, in brief, of five kinds. First, diligence that abandons nothing — bodhisattvas whose diligence never abandons the unsurpassed vow for all beings, nor the effort that carries it out. Second, diligence free of any diminishment — bodhisattvas whose diligence, matching or exceeding what was originally vowed, is diligently applied and continues to grow. Third, diligence free of inferiority — bodhisattvas whose diligence is courageous, blazing, sustained across a long span of time, applied without interruption, the mind never faint-hearted, never wavering. Fourth, diligence free of distortion — bodhisattvas whose diligence genuinely brings about real benefit, sustained through genuinely skilful means. Fifth, diligence of vigorous application — bodhisattvas whose diligence advances swiftly and directly towards supreme, complete awakening.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Kind Diligence Opens — Six Qualities Distilled Into Five Memorable Marks

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切種精進？謂此精進，六種、七種，總十三種。云何菩薩六種精進？一、無間精進。謂一切時修加行故。二、殷重精進。謂能周備修加行故。三、等流精進。謂先因力所任持故。四、加行精進。數數思擇種種善品，正加行故。五、無動精進。一切苦觸不能動故，亦不轉成餘性分故。六、無喜足精進。少分下劣差別證中不喜足故。菩薩成就如是六種一切種精進，發勤精進故，所以說言：有勢、有勤、有勇、堅猛，於諸善法不捨其軛。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind diligence? This diligence is, in brief, of thirteen kinds altogether — six of one sort and seven of another. What are the six kinds? First, diligence without interruption, applying effort at every time. Second, diligence with genuine thoroughness, applying effort in a fully comprehensive way. Third, diligence flowing from prior cause, carried forward by the sustaining power of one's original resolve. Fourth, diligence of genuine application, repeatedly and deliberately reflecting on and choosing wholesome practice, correctly applying effort accordingly. Fifth, diligence that cannot be shaken, unmoved by any painful physical contact, and never lapsing into a lesser vehicle or lower disposition. Sixth, diligence without complacency, never satisfied with any partial or inferior attainment. Bodhisattvas who accomplish these six kinds of comprehensive-kind diligence, having diligently applied themselves, are described as: having strength, having application, having courage, having firm resilience, and never setting down the yoke of wholesome practice.

items.title: Section: Seven More — From Desire-Fuelled Diligence to Extinguishing a Fire on One's Own Head — Comprehensive-Kind Diligence Closes at Thirteen

items.zh: 云何菩薩七種精進？一、與欲俱行精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，數於無上正等菩提，猛利欲願隨長養故。二、平等相應精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，能令隨一根本煩惱及隨煩惱，不染污心、亦不纏心。由此精進，能令菩薩於諸善法等習而住。三、勝進精進。謂諸菩薩，若為隨一根本煩惱及隨煩惱染心、纏心；為斷如是諸煩惱故，精進勇猛，如滅頭然。四、勤求精進。謂諸菩薩勇猛勤求一切明處無厭倦故。五、修學精進。謂諸菩薩，於所學法如應如宜，普於一切法隨法行能成辦故。六、利他精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，於如前說十一種相，應知其相。七、善護精進。謂諸菩薩所有精進，起正加行，善自防守；若有所犯，如法悔除。如是菩薩十三種精進，名一切種精進。
items.en: What are the seven kinds? First, diligence accompanied by longing: bodhisattvas whose diligence repeatedly deepens their intense, genuine longing for supreme awakening. Second, diligence in genuine equanimity: bodhisattvas whose diligence prevents any root or secondary affliction from defiling or entangling the mind, sustaining an even, undisturbed engagement with wholesome practice throughout. Third, decisive diligence: bodhisattvas who, whenever any root or secondary affliction does defile or entangle the mind, apply courageous diligence to eliminate it as urgently as one would extinguish a fire burning on one's own head. Fourth, diligence in eager study: bodhisattvas who tirelessly and courageously pursue mastery of every field of knowledge. Fifth, diligence in genuine practice: bodhisattvas who, according to what is genuinely fitting, actually put into universal practice everything learned, in full accordance with the teaching. Sixth, diligence in benefiting others: bodhisattvas whose diligence should be understood through the eleven aspects already described. Seventh, diligence in careful guarding: bodhisattvas whose diligence properly applies itself and carefully guards their own conduct, and, should any lapse occur, promptly confesses and corrects it in accordance with the teaching. These thirteen kinds of diligence together are called comprehensive-kind diligence.

blocks.text: A short day: diligence as a good person practises it, and its many kinds.

Diligence "that abandons nothing" (Venerable Miào Jìng: with this vow comes this practice); that never diminishes; that is never faint-hearted; never scattered; never proud. Master Cháng Bǎi: even through many lives it does not stop.
Six concern its qualities; seven its expressions.

subs.head: Like a fire on one's head

blocks.text: "To cut off afflictions, they strive courageously, like putting out a fire on one's own head." Diligence accompanied by longing: "repeatedly deepening intense longing for awakening" (Venerable Miào Jìng: longing is the vow). Master Cháng Bǎi: vow and diligence nourish each other.

"Putting out a fire on one's own head" is one of Buddhism's oldest images for urgency. The treatise pairs it with the armour of the previous day: one image for endurance across aeons, one for urgency in the present moment. A practitioner needs both.

quiz.q: The first good-person diligence: "never abandoning the effort of all wishes," rendered "never abandons the actual effort to help every being." Where do the lectures put the emphasis?
options: the emphasis is the vow: Miào Jìng — with such a vow comes such practice; Cháng Bǎi — even if a being remains untamed for many eons, not one thought of abandoning them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: with this vow comes this practice — that is "diligence abandoning nothing." Master Cháng Bǎi: even through many eons for a single being who still will not be guided, there is not one thought of giving up. The English misses the vow at the centre.

quiz.q: "Diligence of superior progress" — what image does the treatise use for the urgency of cutting afflictions?
options: like putting out a fire on one's own head
quiz.why: "To cut off these afflictions, they strive courageously, like putting out a fire on one's own head." Master Cháng Bǎi: as if one's head were on fire right now — one must douse it immediately.

quiz.q: The first of seven, "diligence accompanied by longing" — how do the lectures relate longing and diligence?
options: Miào Jìng: "longing" is the vow — willingness to strive; Cháng Bǎi: vow and diligence nourish each other and advance together
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "longing" is the vow — the will to strive. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva's vow and diligence moisten and nourish each other, advancing together.
